donnees.titre: Optical Coherence Tomography Findings Associated With the Glaucoma-periodontitis Stage
donnees.titre_officiel: Evaluation of the Relationship Between the Stage of Periodontal Disease and Retinal Layer Thicknesses in Glaucoma Patients Using Optical Coherence Tomography
donnees.promoteur: Recep Tayyip Erdogan University Training and Research Hospital
donnees.resume_source:
The aim of this observational study is to investigate the relationship between the stage of periodontal disease and retinal layer thicknesses in glaucoma patients using optical coherence tomography (OCT). The primary question the study seeks to answer is:

Is there a relationship between the stage of periodontal disease and retinal layer thicknesses in glaucoma patients?

Participants-with and without glaucoma and at various stages of periodontal disease-will undergo periodontal examinations and optical coherence tomography (OCT) assessments to evaluate retinal layer thicknesses.

bras.description: Systemically healthy individuals with primary open-angle glaucoma who have normal intraocular pressure (9-21 mmHg)
Systemically healthy individuals with primary open-angle glaucoma who have high intraocular pressure (≥21 mmHg)

eligibilite.criteres:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Men and women aged 60 years and older
* Systemically healthy individuals
* Patients diagnosed with primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) according to the European Glaucoma Society (EGS) 2017 classification

Exclusion Criteria:

* Presence of autoimmune, osteoporotic, or malignant disease
* Chronic use of immunosuppressive drugs, oral contraceptives, or bisphosphonate therapy
* Pregnancy
* Retinal, optic nerve, or choroidal vascular diseases; cataracts, age-related macular degeneration, uveitis, Behçet's disease, or scleritis
* Previous refractive or intraocular surgery
* Active infectious diseases (e.g., tuberculosis, hepatitis, HIV/AIDS)
* Chronic use of medications that may affect periodontal tissues (e.g., cyclosporine A, phenytoin)
